The tool's description says it 'saves without a confirm step', yet a Tier-A card was raised on 5 of 5 runs and nothing was written. Those are not in conflict once the card's nature is right: in the default `write` mode a Tier-A tool raises a PROMPT-ONCE tool_approval card until the user allowlists it, then auto-applies — 'without a confirm step' means no two-phase confirm_token of the kind Tier W uses, not 'no card'. This is the same resolution world_create needed in batch 28, where 'Direct + reversible' looked false for the same reason. Not a defect, and correcting the description would have been the error.

defects.why_it_matters: This is the tool a human editor's saved translation goes through — authored_by='human'. An empty save is not a no-op: it mints a real version that sits in the chapter's version list looking like a human edit, and translation_set_active_version can later publish it to readers. The tool does not auto-activate (it says so, and that held), so nothing is published today — which is exactly why this is a latent gap rather than an incident.
defects.recorded_not_fixed: Recorded rather than fixed in this batch: the fix belongs to translation-service and the loop's CODE bar wants a falsifier proven RED on the original, the owning suite green and a content-verified deploy. Filed here with the exact reproduction so it can be picked up as its own unit.
defects.fixed:
FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-22.
🔴 THE FIRST FIX WAS INERT AND THE LIVE RE-PROBE IS WHAT CAUGHT IT. The validator went on SaveEditedTranslationRequest, whose docstring has always carried this invariant — on the reasoning that the REST handler and the MCP tool both build it. They do not: the MCP tool writes its INSERT directly and never constructs the model. So the fix was deployed, md5-confirmed inside the container, and an empty body STILL saved a version. Guard the CALL SITE, not the helper — the same rule this loop broke earlier the same day when a preflight edit made fe_runner's main() a no-op while the helper's own tests stayed green.
Both are now guarded. Live on the deployed service: translated_body='' and '   ' are REFUSED ('translated_body must not be empty — saving an empty human edit would create a version that looks like a translation and contains nothing'), a real edit still saves, and the chapter ends with exactly the seed + the one real version. 12 falsifier tests, proven RED on the original by removing the guard (5 refusal tests failed, the 4 bystanders stayed green). Full translation suite: 1193 passed, 0 failed.
defects.red_on_original:
PROVEN RED by re-injecting the ORIGINAL defect, then restored by a targeted edit rather than `git checkout` (which would have discarded the fix in the same file). Replacing the model guard's condition with `if False:` took 5 of the refusal tests RED — empty string, whitespace-only, neither-field, empty json list, and the message check — while all 4 BYSTANDER tests (a text edit, a json-block edit, a single character, and whitespace preserved verbatim in what is stored) stayed GREEN. That split is what makes them bystanders rather than four more copies of the same assertion.
The MCP call-site tests are source-level (the handler needs a live pool and a real MCP context), and their RED proof is the LIVE re-probe: with only the model fix deployed and md5-confirmed, an empty body still saved version_num 2 and 3; with the call-site guard deployed, both are refused and a real edit still saves.
defects.invariant:
THE INVARIANT: a tool that CREATES a durable, author-attributed artefact must refuse an EMPTY one. An empty artefact is not a harmless no-op — it is indistinguishable from real content in every listing that shows it, and downstream tools will happily publish it.

WHERE IT IS ENFORCED: at the CALL SITE that writes, not on a shared request model. This defect had two call sites — the REST route (which builds SaveEditedTranslationRequest) and the MCP tool (which writes its INSERT directly) — and guarding only the model left the agent path open while looking fixed. Both now carry it.

PROVED AGAINST EVERY PAST INCIDENT OF THE CLASS this loop has measured, and the record is mixed, which is why the invariant is worth naming rather than assuming:
  * book_steering_set     — an empty body is REFUSED ('body is required'). Correct. (batch 28)
  * world_create          — an empty name is REFUSED ('name is required'). Correct. (batch 28)
  * kg_view_edit          — op=upsert without a name is REFUSED. Correct. (batch 33)
  * world_update          — a call with no fields is REFUSED. Correct. (batch 31)
  * settings_update_profile — a call with no fields is REFUSED. Correct. (batch 35)
  * book_chapter_bulk_create — an empty `chapters` list was recorded as OWED in batch 26 and never     exercised; it is the one remaining member of this class with no evidence either way, and it is the     obvious next probe.
  * translation_save_edited_version — ACCEPTED an empty body. The only measured violation. Fixed here.

WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX: a body that is non-empty but meaningless — one character, or the untouched LLM text saved straight back. Those are real versions by any mechanical test and guessing at them would block edits this tool exists to accept.
